name: supply-sophie-unanswered-round
narrative: Sophie runs RUTF procurement for the Connect-RUTF program. 17 days ago she asked six suppliers to quote tender 2: half have never answered, despite two reminders, and the deadline is four days off, so chasing them is still worth it; and she forwards whatever does arrive to an AI that records it. Sophie opens tender 2 and reads where it stands: collecting quotes with its deadline in 4 days, three of six answered and three silent, each quote recorded from the supplier's own email with the fact it left out, each silent supplier with when she last chased it and a reminder already drafted, and that the tender has not settled how import duty is handled. She opens the reminder drafted for Sahel, which says when Sahel was asked and last reminded, sends it, and marks it sent from the draft itself; no further reminder falls before the deadline. Sahel answers with a quote; Sophie forwards it, and in the tender's history, turned to replies only, Sahel's email comes first: she opens it beside what the AI recorded from it, the reply dated the day it came in. On the comparison, side by side, no quote can be compared yet: the tender's import duty terms are not settled, so Harmattan's carriage-paid quote, which leaves the import to us, waits on them; Kanem has not stated its pack, and Sahel's quote is ex works, so its freight is ours with no freight estimate recorded, and in euros with no exchange rate recorded; our clearing estimate sits on the quotes we import. Back on the tender she settles import duty on its terms line: we import, under the program's duty waiver. Northgate's three questions are still on her, and Reply opens an email drafted with the three questions, an answer to write under each. The comparison then costs the quotes we import under the waiver: Harmattan's becomes comparable, one of three, landed at its quoted price plus our clearing estimate, while Kanem's pack, our freight estimate for Sahel and Sahel's exchange rate are still missing. Importing makes the paperwork hers, and tender 1 shows what that means: its order with Harmattan is at customs, held, waiting on us. Its status view shows nothing received yet, the invoice billed above the agreed price and the days it is late, and On us lists the documents owed to the forwarder and the invoice to review; the forwarder's email in the order's history says the trucks are held at the border on our import permit. Back on her overview, tender 2 reads what changed: three of six answered and none comparable when she opened it, four answered and 1 of 3 comparable, Harmattan, now, its next move hers, the reply to Northgate; the order is hers too, and a RUSF tender she asked two days ago waits on its suppliers, with the moves on her counted against those waiting on suppliers.

sophie.intro: Sophie buys RUTF for the Connect-RUTF program; suppliers and the freight forwarder email her, and she forwards what they send to an AI that records it.
sophie.name: Sophie

scenes.narrative: Sophie asked six suppliers to quote tender 2 and reminded the quiet ones twice. She opens the tender: collecting quotes, its deadline in 4 days, so there is still time to chase; half have answered and three are silent. Each quote that came in is recorded from the supplier's own email, marked as recorded by the AI, and the fact a quote left out is pulled out beside it: Kanem's sachets per carton. Sahel's row, like each silent supplier's, shows when she last chased it, with a reminder already drafted. The terms line says the tender has not settled how import duty is handled.
scenes.title: Half the tender never answered

scenes.narrative: With the deadline four days off, Sophie opens the tender's draft emails at the reminder drafted for Sahel: it says when Sahel was asked and when she last reminded them, and under the message the Sent on field already holds today's date beside Mark sent. Once the reminder has gone she marks it sent, and back on the tender's Invitations Sahel's row is marked: reminder sent today, the third reminder, and no further reminder before the deadline.
scenes.title: She chases Sahel from a drafted reminder

scenes.narrative: Sahel answers the reminder with a quote and Sophie forwards it to the AI. She lands on the tender's history, turned to replies only, where Sahel's email comes first. scenes.title: Sahel finally answers, and she opens the email

features.description: The comparison sets every quote side by side, one row per fact, puts main freight on us for an ex-works quote and our clearing estimate on every quote we import, and marks each fact a quote has not stated, without ranking quotes that cannot be compared; a quote missing a fact stays out of the count whatever the duty terms.

features.description: A line at the top of the comparison states the tender's import duty terms; while they are not settled, every quote whose Incoterm leaves the import to us waits on them.
features.verify: Playwright: [data-testid=comparison-duty-terms] reads 'Import duty: not settled'; Harmattan Therapeutics' [data-testid=grid-status] reads '1 fact on us' and its Next step offers 'Settle duty terms'

scenes.narrative: Sophie opens the comparison, every quote side by side, and none can be compared yet, for more than one reason. The tender's import duty terms are not settled, and Harmattan quotes carriage paid to Kano, which leaves the import to us, so its duty is ours to cost and its column waits on our terms. Each quote's other gaps are marked where they fall: Kanem has not stated its pack, and Sahel's new quote is ex works Niamey, so main freight is ours and our freight estimate is not recorded, and it is in euros, with no exchange rate recorded yet. Our clearing and forwarding estimate, USD 1.20 per carton, sits on both quotes we import; Kanem's delivered-duty-paid quote clears its own. Settling the terms would free only the quotes that leave the import to us; Kanem's pack and Sahel's rate are still owed. A quote that cannot be compared shows no landed figure: its header counts the facts owed by us and by the supplier, and the same gaps appear in its landed cell and as its next steps.
scenes.title: No quote can be compared yet: duty terms unsettled, facts missing

features.verify: Playwright: [data-testid=on-us] contains 'Reply to Northgate Commodities (3 questions)'; its [data-testid=move-cta] opens #drafts at the drafted reply

features.description: After the tender's duty terms are set, the comparison's duty line reads the waiver, the Import duty row is settled for every quote whose Incoterm leaves the import to us, and only the quotes missing no other fact become comparable.

scenes.narrative: Back on the tender, Sophie settles import duty on the tender's terms line: we import, under the program's duty waiver, and the line reads the waiver, just recorded. Northgate's three questions are still on her under On us, and Reply opens an email drafted with the three questions, an answer to write under each. She opens the comparison again: the duty line reads the waiver, the Import duty row is settled for the quotes we import, and Harmattan's quote is now comparable, one of three: its landed figure, USD 51.30 per carton, is its quoted price plus our clearing estimate, and its column marks the waiver document not on file as a fact on us, so Award is offered but not yet the filled button; Kanem's and Sahel's still wait on their missing facts.
scenes.title: She settles the tender's duty terms and replies to Northgate

scenes.narrative: Importing makes the paperwork hers, and tender 1 shows what that means: its order with Harmattan for 2,000 cartons is at customs, held, waiting on us. The status view shows nothing received yet, the invoice billed above the agreed price, and the days late split between the supplier's and ours; On us lists the documents owed to the forwarder, to mark provided, and the invoice, to pay or dispute. The invoice's lines read billed against agreed, what we owe to clear the shipment lists the import permit and the customs declaration, each to mark provided, and the forwarder's email in the order's history says the trucks are held at the border until the permit is lodged.
scenes.title: Tender 1's order: held on our permit, billed high

features.verify: Playwright: tender 2's [data-testid=row-stage] contains 'Collecting quotes', its [data-testid=row-comparable] reads '1 of 3 comparable · Harmattan', and its [data-testid=whose] contains 'Us'; the RUSF tender's [data-testid=row-stage] contains 'Collecting quotes' and its [data-testid=whose] contains 'Suppliers'

scenes.narrative: Back on her overview, tender 2 reads what changed since she opened it: then three of six had answered and no quote was comparable; now four have answered, Northgate with questions rather than a quote, and the chip leading its stage reads 1 of 3 comparable, Harmattan. What the other quotes still miss sits under its next move as outlined facts, apart from the moves. Its next move is hers: reply to Northgate's three questions. The moves on us are counted against those waiting on suppliers, each row carrying its own: a RUSF tender for Maiduguri, asked two days ago, waits on its suppliers, and the tender 1 order at customs is hers.
scenes.title: Whose move each procurement is, ours or the suppliers'
